comments.body:
Archaeology summary (2026-09-06): I did not find an earlier infra plan approving a CPU instance-family/monthly-spend Option C for resizing this host. The “Option C” I found is ADR 0112 / ticket livid-blondish-shearwater: review-gate scratch moves to a dedicated EBS volume; its S0 ticket says the operator approved “Option A + Option C” for disk-ceiling architecture, but that is disk isolation, not EC2 CPU sizing, and it carries no monthly-dollar cap. ADR 0104 and ADR 0112 only say the MCP blue/green overlap should not force t4g.large -> t4g.xlarge; ADR 0112 explicitly records host sizing was not reopened.

Numbers found: current t4g.large on-demand/mo is recorded on cultivated-unfriended-nene as $49.06; r7g.large is $78.18 and explicitly “approved ceiling” there. The older op-cert budget evidence on sonic-columned-sturgeon / decisive-anarthrous-oryx says the June AWS bill was $90.94 total and the prior binding constraint was zero fixed-monthly-cost increase on the existing t4g.large box. Current CPU incident evidence here and on antihuman-beefwitted-zebra: CPUCreditBalance hit/stayed 0.0 with surplus credits accruing; later recovery comment here says there is still no CPUCreditBalance alarm.

Verdict: needs-user-decision for t4g.xlarge/m7g.large, because I found no approved Option-C dollar cap that covers those CPU-sizing choices. If staying within recorded approval, cultivated-unfriended-nene already chooses r7g.large ($78.18/mo, non-burstable, 16 GiB) and treats any more vCPU as a separate cost decision. Escalation text: “I found approved disk Option C, not an approved CPU-resize Option C. Known figures: current t4g.large $49.06/mo; approved W3 ceiling r7g.large $78.18/mo; historical total AWS bill $90.94. Do you approve a CPU-focused resize to t4g.xlarge or m7g.large, or should we proceed with r7g.large plus a CPUCreditBalance alarm?”

compiled_state.description:
## Summary

The Gerrit host `i-00880b2c7f13527c5` is a **burstable `t4g.large`** (2 vCPU / 7.8 GiB) whose
**CPU credit balance has been exhausted since 12:38 UTC on 2026-09-05** and has stayed at zero.
It is now running entirely on billed surplus credits, which are accruing. This is a structural
instance-sizing and cost finding, distinct from the proxy-timeout defect it was discovered under.

Discovered while root-causing `antihuman-beefwitted-zebra` (`5bba-45dd-3bfc-42f1`). Raising the
nginx read timeout stops the 504s; it does **not** address this. The host remains short of CPU.

## Measurements (CloudWatch, `AWS/EC2`, instance `i-00880b2c7f13527c5`, 1h Average)

**`CPUCreditBalance`** — steady decline through 2026-09-04, hits zero and stays there:

```
2026-09-04 15:38 PT  352.9      2026-09-05 02:38 PT   74.9
2026-09-04 18:38 PT  281.1      2026-09-05 03:38 PT   31.6
2026-09-04 21:38 PT  166.2      2026-09-05 04:38 PT   13.7
2026-09-05 01:38 PT  116.3      2026-09-05 05:38 PT    0.0   <- exhausted (12:38 UTC)
                                2026-09-05 06:38..14:38 PT  0.0  (10 further hours at zero)
```

**`CPUSurplusCreditBalance`** — climbing continuously since exhaustion, i.e. accruing charges:

```
05:38 PT  15.5    07:38 PT  40.7    09:38 PT 117.0    11:38 PT 206.0    13:38 PT 281.1
06:38 PT  20.1    08:38 PT  78.9    10:38 PT 168.3    12:38 PT 254.4    14:38 PT 316.7
```

**`CPUUtilization`** — sustained **55-74%** across the day against a **30% baseline** for
`t4g.large`. The instance is in `unlimited` mode (`describe-instance-credit-specifications`
returns `unlimited`), so it is not hard-throttled yet, but it is running roughly 2x its
entitlement continuously and paying for the difference.

**On-host corroboration:**

- `vmstat` showed CPU `steal` reaching **13%**.
- Load average **9-12 on 2 vCPU** (`/proc/loadavg`: `9.49 9.04 9.81`, later `12.61 11.33 10.55`).
- Gerrit `git-upload-pack` requests spend only **~24% of wall time on CPU** (median over 37
  anonymous CI fetches from `/var/gerrit/logs/httpd_log`) — off-CPU ~76% of the time. A full
  clone needs ~20-28s of CPU and takes 85-144s of wall.
- Memory: `free -m` showed 202 MB free of 7813, **no swap**, `kswapd0` active, page cache
  squeezed to ~600-714 MB on a git server.

**Correlation with the 504 incidents:** all four `Gerrit Verified Gate` checkout failures on
2026-09-05 (15:38, 15:39, 21:52, 22:08 UTC) occurred **after** the credit balance hit zero at
12:38 UTC. The earlier cluster (02:51-03:08 UTC) occurred while the balance was collapsing
(74.9 -> 31.6 -> 13.7).

## Largest single consumer — and what is NOT established about it

`ps` on the host: **`rebar-mcp` at 4.45 GB RSS (55.6% of RAM) and 47% CPU**, against Gerrit's JVM
at 765 MB RSS / 3.3% and the review-bot at 746 MB / 4.1%.

**NOT ESTABLISHED:** that `rebar-mcp`'s footprint *causes* the credit exhaustion. It is the
largest consumer by a wide margin, which is correlation. It has not been shown to be a leak rather
than steady state, and no measurement attributes a share of credit burn to it.

**Re-measure before acting on that number.** Change **2685** merged tonight — a per-ticket
projection in `reduce_all_tickets`, measured to cut whole-store read cost from ~295 MB to ~84 MB
per concurrent call. **It has not been deployed to the host**, so the 4.45 GB above predates it.
Whoever picks this up should take a fresh reading after that deploy rather than inheriting this
figure.

## Why this is worth its own ticket

Raising the nginx `proxy_read_timeout` (bug `5bba`) stops the 504s by no longer converting slow-
but-successful responses into errors. It leaves untouched the reason those responses are slow. A
host at zero credits with sustained 2x-baseline utilisation will keep degrading every latency-
sensitive surface on it — Gerrit git serving, the review-bot's voting (`voter_errors`), the MCP
service, the observability probe — and will keep costing surplus charges.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 A fresh `CPUCreditBalance` / `CPUSurplusCreditBalance` / `CPUUtilization` reading is
      taken AFTER change 2685 is deployed, so the decision rests on current data.
- [ ] AC2 The credit burn is attributed across tenants (Gerrit JVM, rebar-mcp, review-bot,
      opcert, autodeploy, observability) rather than assumed, so the remedy targets the actual
      consumer.
- [ ] AC3 A decision is recorded between the available remedies, with its cost basis: move to a
      non-burstable instance class, resize, reduce tenancy (move build/gate work off the Gerrit
      host), or accept `unlimited` surplus charges as the steady state.
- [ ] AC4 Because the approved remedy is non-burstable `r7g.large`, a `CPUUtilization` alarm exists for sustained host CPU saturation; no `CPUCreditBalance` alarm is added because r7g has no burst-credit signal.
- [ ] AC5 Whether `rebar-mcp`'s RSS is a leak or steady state is settled by measurement.

## Constraints

Production is read-only for investigation; instance-class changes are operator-authorized and must
follow a reviewed plan. Never use `--force` or any gate bypass.

## Operator-Approved Execution Frame (2026-09-07)
Operator approval is recorded in comments: prior archaeology found `cultivated-unfriended-nene` approved `r7g.large` at $78.18/month, and this ticket is approved to execute that resize. The earlier plan noise was merged-but-unapplied main config, not foreign drift: antelope applied those merged-main user_data/observability changes first, so this ticket's fresh plan is now isolated to the approved resize plus this ticket's CPUUtilization alarm.

Fresh Terraform plan envelope from `infra/terraform` after antelope apply:

- `create aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm.ec2_cpu_utilization_high` (`replace=[]`) — salamander's non-burstable CPU saturation alarm; CPUCreditBalance is not meaningful on r7g.
- `update aws_instance.gerrit` (`replace=[]`) — instance type changes from `t4g.large` to approved `r7g.large`.
- `0 destroy`, `0 replace`.

Stop condition: any destroy, replacement, or non-no-op resource outside the two entries above stops the apply. Provider-computed instance attributes may refresh as part of the in-place instance update, but the intended mutable field is `instance_type` only.

Rollback/back-out: keep `rebar-autodeploy.timer` disabled while unhealthy. Revert `var.instance_type` to `t4g.large`, re-run/apply the rollback plan, allow the required stop/start, then require Gerrit `/config/server/version`, review-bot `/review/health`, and MCP `/mcp/` response to recover before re-enabling autodeploy.
